en: How many of us are really sure what's in Antarctica?
This map from 1513 shows a continent no one saw until 1820.
Ottoman Admiral Piri Reis drew it on Gazelskin.
It surfaced in 1929 in Topkapi Palace.
Writers saw Antarctica in its southern coast, mapped before the ice by a lost civilization.
But that ice is millions of years old.
Historians see South America there, bent east to fit the skin.
His notes list about 20 maps, one drawn by Columbus.
His uncle, the Corsair Kemal Reis, held a captive who sailed with Columbus three times.
He copied the old maps wonders too.
Monks on a giant fish, one-horned oxen, monsters seven spams long.
He even noted that they are harmless souls.
Columbus's own map was never found.
And under that ice like fossil forests, even dinosaurs, we still know so little
So how can we be so sure?
